pick.headline: US hostages freed from Iran
pick.summary: On 20 January 1981, minutes after Ronald Reagan was sworn in, the 52 Americans held in Iran for 444 days were flown out of Tehran.
pick.significance: The hostage crisis had broken Carter's presidency and changed US policy toward Iran for decades. Among the hostages were CIA officers whose presence Iran had used as propaganda.

alternates.headline: Terry Waite disappears in Beirut
alternates.summary: On 20 January 1987 Terry Waite, the Archbishop of Canterbury's envoy who had been negotiating for the release of Western hostages, was seized in Beirut.
alternates.significance: Waite had unknowingly been entangled in the arms-for-hostages dealings exposed weeks earlier as the Iran-Contra affair. He was held for nearly five years.

alternates.headline: Soviet troops storm Baku
alternates.summary: In the night of 19-20 January 1990 Soviet troops forced their way into Baku under a state of emergency, killing more than a hundred people.
alternates.significance: The crackdown, ordered after anti-Armenian pogroms and a nationalist challenge to Communist rule, turned Azerbaijani opinion decisively against Moscow.
